JustCo Place in Orchard secures 80% retail leasing commitment ahead of opening
article:
Co-working, co-living and retail development JustCo Place at 160 Orchard Road has secured leasing commitments for 80% of its retail podium as it gears up to debut the retail podium and co-living apartments in the coming months.

The retail tenant mix spans global brands, concepts that are new to Singapore or the region, and homegrown businesses in F&B, lifestyle and wellness.

Under the fitness and wellness offerings, the committed tenant line-up includes New York performance training brand AARMY; UK fitness brand Karve, which will focus on Pilates; Singapore martial arts name Evolve MMA Orchard’s flagship academy, which is taking up 10,000 sq ft; and hair salon SO Salon.

F&B players include Michelin Bib Gourmand Korean restaurant brand Gwanghwamun Mijin, Surrey Hills Grocer’s first flagship bakery The Hills Bakehouse, Shanghai’s minimalist specialty coffee brand M Stand, Chinese hotpot chain Chamoon Royale, social dining bar and bistro Helen’s, as well as 160 Coffeehouse, a new local coffee concept created for JustCo Place.

Meanwhile, entertainment tenants include homegrown KTV brand K.Star Karaoke, and an escape room by live entertainment firm Fever.

The line-up “reflects JustCo’s approach to curating concepts around how people increasingly work, live, connect and spend their time, while remaining relevant to the lifestyles of Singapore’s consumers”, said the Singapore-listed flexible workspace operator in a Nov 5 bourse filing.

At the Orchard property, retailers are set to progressively start operating from this December onwards.

The co-living component under the Just At brand is expected to open in 2027, with 123 fully furnished apartments across Levels 6 to 10. JustCo will operate this serviced apartment tower under an asset-light management contract signed with OG.

On Levels 3 and 4, the co-working centre opened in September with full occupancy.

“With the coworking centre fully occupied, strong progress in retail leasing and the development of Just At underway, the different parts of the ‘work, live, connect’ ecosystem are steadily coming together,” said Kong Wan Sing, CEO of JustCo.

The development, owned by OG , formerly housed Taste Orchard and OG’s department store.

title: AI elite lose US$18 bil as chip stock rout spreads to Asia
article:
(Nov 6): SoftBank Group Corp founder Masayoshi Son and other tycoons across Asia saw billions erased from their fortunes as a global tech sell-off rippled through their companies on Friday.

Twenty-two billionaires from China, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea who rank in the world’s 500 richest lost more than US$21 billion ($27 billion) in combined wealth as of 10am Hong Kong time, before paring that to more than US$18 billion, according to calculations from the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Son was the biggest loser, with his fortune declining by US$3.9 billion to about US$29 billion.

Among the hardest hit were the firms at the heart of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. Those who lost US$1 billion or more include Takemitsu Takizaki of electronic sensor maker Keyence Corp, and Singapore’s richest person Jason Chang of ASE Technology Holding Co, which assembles and packages semiconductors.

Samsung Electronics Co shareholders Jay Y Lee, his mother and sister — one of Asia’s richest families — collectively lost about US$2.5 billion from their fortunes.

The turmoil also last month hit hedge funds including Tiger Global Management and Whale Rock Capital Management, as concerns over AI investments roiled markets. In Asia, wealthy clients of brokers from Taiwan to Hong Kong faced margin calls on leveraged bets, people familiar with the matter said.

Expectations that a Democrat-controlled House of Representatives and Senate will work to slow construction of data centres — a critical component of AI infrastructure — helped drive technology stocks lower across Asia on Friday, following a record US$2.3 trillion wipeout in market value of the Nasdaq 100 index. The losses extended a wealth reversal that saw Nvidia Corp’s Jensen Huang drop out of the world’s top 10 richest.

See also: OpenAI to change how it handles data centres after outcry

title: Trump-linked crypto firm plans token buyback after midterm rout
article:
(Nov 6): The Trump family crypto venture World Liberty Financial has announced a new buyback plan for its WLFI token after the price fell following this week’s US midterm elections.

Cryptocurrencies whipsawed following initial results from Tuesday’s election, showing Democrats would retake control of both chambers of Congress next year. Tokens linked to Republican President Donald Trump were hit by a particularly acute selloff.

WLFI tokens have fallen about 8% since election night and are down more than 70% from their high this year, according to CoinGecko data. The selloff has put fresh focus on how the Trump family’s crypto ventures have become intertwined with the president’s political fortunes. The buyback plan could provide support for the token’s price as it grapples with this week’s election fallout.

“The goal is to encourage active participation in WLFI governance and consolidate voting power among our most committed long-term holders,” World Liberty Financial said in a post on X Thursday. WLFI allows holders to vote on proposals governing the protocol, with more tokens conferring greater voting power, subject to applicable limits.

About 32% of WLFI’s 100 billion maximum token supply is currently in circulation, according to CoinGecko.

See also: Binance loses market share to crypto exchange rivals after hack

The buyback will initially be funded through an allocation that may include fees earned from reserves backing the project’s USD1 stablecoin and other sources, World Liberty said in its post. The company did not disclose the size of the initial allocation or a timeline for purchases, but said buybacks would become “an ongoing part of our long-term strategy with the pace and scale” determined by ecosystem growth and participation.

World Liberty didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment sent outside US working hours.

The company has previously bought back WLFI, including through a buyback-and-burn program after the token began trading publicly in September 2025.

See also: North Korea’s hackers supercharge crypto heists with AI skills

World Liberty was co-founded by Donald Trump and his sons, among other business partners, in the weeks before the 2024 election. DT Marks DEFI LLC, an entity affiliated with the president and members of his family, owns about 38% of World Liberty’s holding company, according to a disclosure on the website. The family also holds WLFI tokens, with economic interests tied to sales of the token and reserves backing the USD1 stablecoin, according to company disclosures.

The latest buyback plan comes at a sensitive time for the project as it faces a tougher political climate and a prolonged decline in its governance token.

Trump’s financial exposure to crypto has drawn scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers, raising questions about conflicts of interest as the administration has pushed an industry-friendly agenda. The president’s US$1.4 billion haul last year from crypto-related ventures, with about US$594 million of that coming from World Liberty sales, intensified concerns when it was disclosed in June.

title: Singapore arrests and charges key aide of alleged scam kingpin
article:
(Nov 6): A key Singaporean associate of alleged global scam kingpin Chen Zhi was charged in court on Friday, as authorities continue their crackdown more than a year after the US and UK unmasked what they called a transnational criminal empire.

Chen Xiuling, also known as Karen Chen, was detained by Singapore police on Thursday upon her return to the city state. Authorities had issued a warrant for her arrest earlier this year, and said in March that they believed she was in Cambodia, where Chen Zhi’s Prince Group is based. Chen Zhi and Karen Chen have no familial ties.

The 44-year-old was charged with instigating another person to falsify accounts and with attempted cheating. Both alleged actions related to Singapore-registered companies that she was a director of, which authorities said were beneficially owned by the Prince Group founder. The maximum penalties for the offenses are fines and prison terms of up to 10 years.

Karen Chen is the fourth Singapore citizen that local police have arrested in connection with the Prince Group saga. In October last year, the US and UK announced sanctions against Chen Zhi and numerous companies and individuals linked to him and his conglomerate. Karen Chen was among the 18 individuals named by the US Treasury Department. Around the same time, the US indicted China-born Chen Zhi and accused him of being the mastermind of a massive scam syndicate that allegedly stole money from people all over the world and laundered billions of dollars. Sanctions against more individuals and companies linked to the group were announced in June and this week.

Chen Zhi was arrested in Cambodia in January and extradited to China. The unravelling of his empire has led to a broader crackdown on scam organisations in Cambodia and multiple governments scrutinising the group’s footprints across the world.

In Singapore, authorities have so far seized or frozen more than $700 million worth of assets linked to Chen and Prince, including properties and bank accounts.

See also: Vivian Balakrishnan visits Indonesia after natural gas cuts

Chen Zhi previously had a family office in Singapore and spent significant time in the island nation prior to his arrest. Karen Chen managed the accounts and finances of the family office, and according to the US Treasury, also oversaw numerous Prince Group companies based in Singapore, Mauritius and Taiwan.

According to the latest Singapore charges, she allegedly instigated an officer at a local company called Capital Zone Warehousing Pte to falsify a lease agreement in 2022. She was also accused of attempting to cheat a government agency into approving the takeover of a property’s lease by submitting that fake agreement to it.

Thong Chee Kun, her lawyer, said at a court hearing on Friday morning that his client was in police custody “because she wants to cooperate”. Karen Chen appeared via video link from a holding facility, showed little emotion and said she wanted to assist authorities but also would like to “go home and rest”.

See also: Singapore must work faster to vie with wealth hubs, says deputy PM

She did not submit a plea and was dressed in a black “I Love Paris & Balenciaga” shirt that was also worn during her earlier arrest. A judge denied her bail after the prosecution sought to remand her for about a week, citing the risk of her absconding and communicating with other people.

title: Thailand EV tax gets carmakers weighing more local production
article:
(Nov 6): Thailand’s higher taxes on imported electric vehicles are prompting automakers to consider more local production, boosting Bangkok’s drive to become an EV manufacturing hub.

Millennium Group Corporation (Asia) Pcl, which distributes XPeng vehicles in Thailand, is studying a potential factory with the Chinese automaker after the government announced a 35% excise tax on imported EVs. “We are working with XPeng to assess the project’s commercial viability, potential production volumes, the readiness of local parts suppliers and our ability to meet local-content requirements,” it said in an emailed statement.

Thailand is trying to defend its position as Southeast Asia’s biggest auto-production base as Chinese EVs reshape a market long dominated by Japanese carmakers. EV investment approved by the Board of Investment has nearly doubled in five years, reaching more than 141 billion baht as of September, underscoring the scale of the industry’s shift towards electric vehicles.

Chinese automakers already producing in Thailand are also expanding their local footprint. Omoda & Jaecoo (Thailand) Co plans to increase output and use more domestic components. “We will continue to develop a more complete business ecosystem around our operations in the country,” Vice President Bill Zhang said in an emailed response to Bloomberg News.

Industry officials expect the tax changes to push more manufacturers in the same direction. “Instead of saying they plan to invest, they will move faster to produce vehicles in Thailand,” said Surapong Paisitpattanapong, a spokesman for the Federation of Thai Industries’ Automotive Industry Club, on Thursday.

Under the new structure, fully imported EVs would face a 35% tax, while locally made models would be charged less depending on how much they source domestically. Thailand also plans to tighten those local-content rules in three years, requiring about 40% of a vehicle’s value to come from parts actually made in the country.

See also: Singapore, Johor and Riau Islands triangle is ‘strategic insurance’, says energy expert

The measures are also drawing interest from manufacturers that have yet to commit to local production. Two automakers have sought talks about setting up factories since the changes were approved, Permanent Secretary for Finance Lavaron Sangsnit told reporters on Thursday. AAS Auto Service Co has approached the finance minister, while another company is due to meet the Excise Department this week.

Bangkok wants locally made cars to account for 70% of supply within two years, more than double their share in the first nine months of 2026. The target follows a surge in imports, with China accounting for 96% of Thailand’s EV shipments during that period.

Importers are now accelerating shipments before the higher tax takes effect Jan 1, Surapong said. EV sales are running at roughly double the monthly pace last year, and the FTI’s automotive club expects annual sales to reach about 200,000 vehicles in 2026.

See also: Indonesia’s investor troubles deepen, but opportunities remain

The shift, however, could come at a cost for buyers. Imported models may become significantly more expensive, depending on how much of the added tax automakers absorb to protect market share.

“With the new tax, they could cost 700,000 to 800,000 baht,” said Duangjai Singkul, a Grab driver in Bangkok. “That’s extremely expensive for middle-income people like me.”

title: South Korea’s US$1.7 tril rout burns day traders, challenges Lee
article:
(Nov 6): South Korea’s government turned the world’s hottest stock market into a political trophy. Now, a reversal that’s wiped out more than a trillion dollars in value is stirring a retail investor backlash and testing public faith in its leaders.

Frustration is acute among individuals who say they heeded the government’s call to favour the equity market over real estate, as officials championed the Kospi’s artificial intelligence (AI)-fuelled surge to a record high in June. As things stand, the benchmark has plummeted over 40% since then amid an unravelling global tech rally, while property prices in Seoul have climbed for a record 91 straight weeks.

On Friday, as the Kospi slumped below the 5,000 level that President Lee Jae Myung touted during his election campaign, retail investors vented frustration and mocked Lee’s pledge on online stock forums.

The contrast between share-market performance and property prices has proved particularly painful for Kim Min, a salaried worker in Seoul. Kim says he deferred a decision to buy a house in early 2026, and instead put 40 million won (US$29,500 or $37,774) in an exchange-traded fund (ETF) tied to small-cap Kosdaq gauge. About seven months on, more than 65% of that investment has been wiped out, he claims.

“Looking back, I think it was just pure madness that the government has fueled this rally,” the 40-year-old said. “If I can just get my money back, I would never ever trade Korean stocks again. Never.”

Lee, who took power in June 2025, made shifting household wealth away from real estate and into equities a centrepiece of his economic agenda. His administration tightened mortgage lending and sought to curb speculation in the housing market to restrain property investment, while also taking steps to boost shareholder returns.

See also: Grab to cut Vietnam driver fees, pay compensation after review

During his campaign, Lee pledged to lift the Kospi to 5,000, or about double its level at the time, tying his administration’s credibility closely to the market’s performance. In April 2026, Jung Chung-rae, then chief of the ruling Democratic Party, said the Kospi could reach 8,000.

While the AI boom saw the index shatter those levels to hit a record 9,114.55, a punishing sell-off in July — which marked its worst month in nearly two decades — and another bruising slide in October have shaken retail investors. The Kospi plunged as much as 8.8% on Friday to 4,911.28, before paring about half the loss. That followed a 5.3% slump on Thursday.

See also: Hackers paid US$15 to drain US$2.5 billion from Binance in one hit

“The president went out there and made a very confident case to the public: don’t put your money into real estate, invest in stocks instead,” said Koo Jeong-woo, a sociology professor at Sungkyunkwan University in Seoul. “But a lot of people who followed that advice have now lost money.”

The presidential office declined to comment for this story.

The latest declines in the Kospi have come amid a sell-off in tech stocks globally due to growing concern that Democrats will seek tighter regulation of the AI industry after their strong showing in the US midterms. That could potentially slow the expansion of US data centres and weigh on the demand outlook for South Korean chipmakers.

Overall, about US$1.7 trillion has been eroded from the market value of South Korean stocks since a peak of US$5.1 trillion on June 22, data compiled by Bloomberg showed. That’s before taking into account Friday’s losses.

For South Korean daytraders, the grievance is that the government made the Kospi’s rise a showcase for its economic agenda even as much of the rally was being powered by the broader AI boom.

“There were celebrations at every milestone with photo ceremonies, and people who saw them thought the market would go up really high,” said Kim, the salaried worker from Seoul.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Many retail investors took on debt to enter the market, with brokerage iM Securities Co estimating that more than US$60 billion of stocks were bought while the Kospi traded above 7,000, mostly by mom-and-pop investors. Some piled into leveraged ETFs tied to chip stocks, which can magnify gains but also amplify losses. Those funds are down more than 70% from their peaks.

A mid-October poll showed that the disapproval rating for Lee rose to 52% from 51%. Among those who disapproved, 19% cited the government’s housing policy while 12% cited the state of the economy and response to the stock market as reasons.

Another fallout of the rout may be that retail investors are turning their backs on local stocks, complicating the government’s efforts to discourage outflows as a way to support the South Korean won. South Koreans bought about US$13 billion worth of US stocks in the four months through October, while selling a net US$1.7 billion of Kospi shares in the period, according to depository data.

To be sure, under Lee, South Korea has implemented a series of corporate governance reforms to reduce the so-called Korea Discount, and that supported the Kospi’s world-beating ascent. His administration has also sought to dismantle excessive regulation and inefficiencies in capital markets. The Kospi is still up more than 20% this year.

As the AI frenzy intensified earlier in the year, Wall Street banks including Goldman Sachs Group Inc and JPMorgan Chase & Co were among those that boosted their Kospi targets to at least 12,000.

Now, the same global forces that propelled the index are working in reverse, as concerns mount over lofty valuations and whether the billions of dollars being poured into the technology will bring sufficient returns. Goldman last month cut its target to 9,000.

“Reinvigorating the stock market can be a government’s goal but proposing a number such as 5,000 or 8,000 as the goal could leave a wrong impression,” said Kang In Soo, an economics professor at Sookmyung Women’s University. Now, the Kospi’s sharp fall from over 9,000 will likely dominate public memory, rather than Lee’s election campaign target of 5,000, he said.

title: Hong Kong bourse operator's profit falls as AI scrutiny hits listings, trading
article:
(Nov 6): Hong Kong’s exchange operator unexpectedly posted a decline in profit in the third quarter as an initial public offering (IPO) boom and trading ran into headwinds fuelled by concerns over massive investments to fund the build-out of artificial intelligence (AI).

In the first drop since early 2024, net income at Hong Kong Exchanges & Clearing Ltd fell 1% from a year earlier to HK$4.9 billion ($800.8 million) in the period, according to an exchange filing on Friday, missing the average analyst estimate of HK$5.03 billion. Core business revenue held steady at HK$7.47 billion.

“As we navigate heightened macro uncertainties and ongoing volatility, our conviction in building a deeper and more diverse multi-asset ecosystem has only strengthened,” chief executive officer Bonnie Chan said in the statement.

The results end a streak of record-breaking quarters driven by technology and AI-related debuts. While Hong Kong’s listing pipeline remains active with more than 400 companies waiting in the wings, investor sentiment is beginning to cool amid broader scrutiny of AI valuations and China’s economic outlook.

The rate of abandoned listings has surged to its highest level since the global financial crisis, with about a quarter of planned offerings this year failing to reach completion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

Beijing is also said to be tightening scrutiny of listed company spin-offs, potentially curtailing a key pipeline of IPOs. At the same time, China’s crackdown on illicit cross-border securities trading and concerns over a potential wealth tax are curbing equity turnover.

See also: Hong Kong chip IPOs tap intertwined networks of investors and bosses

Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission has stepped up oversight of IPO bookbuilding practices to root out inflated demand, while probing suspected share rigging tied to one of the city’s most high-profile recent debuts.

HKEX’s shares fell 3% in the early afternoon session on Friday. The city’s benchmark slid 1.1% amid a global sell-off.

From July to September, headline average daily trading at HKEX dropped 11% “against a backdrop of more cautious market sentiment amid inflation concerns, uncertainty over US interest rates and weaker momentum in AI-related stocks”, HKEX said.

See also: Chinese firm’s investor dispute shows dark side of HK listings

Southbound trading of Stock Connect, where Chinese investors buy and sell Hong Kong stocks, slumped 30% from a year earlier to HK$107.3 billion a day. Northbound trading rose 15% during the same period.

A total of 118 companies debuted in the first nine months this year, raising a combined HK$388.4 billion and pushing HKEX to become the second-largest IPO market globally.

HKEX reported nine-month capital expenditure of HK$2.48 billion on acquiring new office space, and another HK$1.47 billion to develop and upgrade trading and clearing systems, and renovation of office premises, it said. Capital expenditure rose 29% in the first nine months.

title: Grab to cut Vietnam driver fees, pay compensation after review
article:
(Nov 5): Grab Holdings Ltd will reduce the fees it collects from drivers in Vietnam and pay about 3.9 billion dong (US$151,854 or $195,026) in compensation for past excessive deductions, following a review by the country’s competition watchdog.

The company will cut the maximum combined platform and app usage fees it retains from drivers to 32%, down from as much as 40.6% for motorbike rides and 39.81% for car trips, the National Competition Commission said in a statement on Thursday.

The ride-hailing firm will also compensate drivers for deductions that exceeded 35% of their revenue share, covering about 0.13% of rides since 2024. The reimbursement starts on Thursday with active drivers receiving payments directly into their Grab wallets, while former drivers will be asked to provide bank details to receive their share, the statement said.

The changes follow complaints from drivers about declining fares and high operating costs, which have put pressure on their take-home earnings. In September, some Grab drivers called for a two-day boycott of the platform to protest what they described as excessive commissions that threatened their ability to earn a living wage.

Alongside the refunds, Grab proposed a broader package of incentives estimated at about 2.95 trillion dong. From Nov. 10, the company will reduce platform fees charged to passengers on selected short-distance trips. It also plans to allocate 860 billion dong for driver bonuses and operational cost support in the fourth quarter, including fuel and electric vehicle charging assistance.

“These changes are intended to support driver-partner earnings opportunities, boost passenger demand and improve transparency,” Grab said in a statement responding to questions from Bloomberg News. “With different countries operating their own regulatory frameworks, we will continue to engage with governments to find ways to support driver-partners, keep rides accessible and maintain reliable services.”

See also: Hackers paid US$15 to drain US$2.5 billion from Binance in one hit

The company attributed the previous excessive deductions to fluctuations in supply and demand, or algorithm errors that caused fees to exceed the system’s prescribed limits, the commission statement said.

The dispute underscores the growing importance of ride-hailing platforms in Vietnam’s urban transport market, where thousands of drivers depend on the services for a living. Vietnam has around 800,000 ride-hailing drivers, who earn on average about nine million dong, around US$350, per month after expenses while working eight to 13 hours a day, according to state media.

title: Malaysia's ex-PM Najib settles RM50 mil fine, paving way for house arrest in SRC case
article:
KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 6): Imprisoned former Malaysian prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has paid the RM50 million ($15.8 million) fine, paving the way to him serving the remainder of his prison term in the confinement of his home.

Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, the secretary general of the Umno party, confirmed the matter via a statement on Friday.

"Umno wishes to announce that the total amount of funds collected through the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund, which was launched on Sept 18 to assist [Najib], has reached its target and is sufficient," the statement said, confirming that the process had been completed at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on Friday.

While voicing their gratitude to all supporters, the party which Najib used to lead until his defeat at the polls in 2018 said that they will be shutting down the special Najib Razak Solidarity Fund.

Najib's lawyer Muhammad Farhan Shafee and the former prime minister's aide Ahmad Lufti Azhar were seen at the payment counter in court around noon on Friday.

The situation was chaotic at the court premises, with reporters chasing the duo between the payment counter and the High Court registration counter for criminal cases where the paperwork was expected to be finalised.

See also: Malaysia's Pardons Board defers decision on ex-PM Najib to future meeting

The press had approached the duo several times to comment but were merely acknowledged with smiles.

Sources close to the matter also confirmed with The Edge that the payment has been made.

However, any other details were scarce at press time.

What is to transpire after the fine payment, in relation Najib's house arrest, is not immediately clear.

Rumour has been rife in recent days that the RM50 million fine would be settled, paving the way for Najib to serve the remainder of his imprisonment in the confines of his home.

Lawyer Muhammad Farhan Shafee (centre) and the former prime minister's aide Ahmad Lufti Azhar (right) on Friday.

Earlier on Friday, Najib's wife Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor — who was in court for one of her own cases — said that neither she nor her family had any knowledge of payments to be made.

Utusan Malaysia had also reported on Friday morning that two representatives of Najib were allegedly seen leaving the payment counter.

On Sept 18, it was announced that the Federal Territory Pardons Board — under the King, Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar — had allowed Najib to serve the remainder of his reduced jail term under house arrest with the caveat that he pays the RM50 million fine first.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Following this, Umno announced that they would crowdfund the sum to help its former party chief.

Najib's lead defence counsel Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah had also previously said that his client does not have the money at hand to pay the fine as his assets remain are under freezing orders and enforcement proceedings.

In the SRC case, the court had upheld Najib's guilty verdict for abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering as well as his 12-year jail term and RM210 million fine.

However, in 2024, the Pardons Board under then-King Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah reduced these to six years and RM50 million.

Najib began serving his jail term on Aug 23, 2022. Following the reduction, he is slated to end his imprisonment in August 2028.

title: SIA to invest over $2 bil in new long-haul cabin products
article:
The products will be featured across all cabins in SIA’s upcoming Boeing 777-9 widebody aircraft, while the 41 retrofitted Airbus 350-900 long-haul and Airbus A350-900 ultra-long-range (ULR) aircraft will feature the new business class seats. The first class cabins will be introduced on the Airbus A350-900 ULR fleet for the first time.

The upgrades will cost the airline over $2 billion and will be progressively introduced from the second half of 2027. The sum includes the previously-announced $1.1 billion plan to retrofit 41 Airbus 350-900 long-haul and ULR aircraft in November 2024.

This will be the airline’s “most comprehensive upgrade” given that the changes go beyond a single aircraft type, says SIA’s chief commercial officer Lee Lik Hsin in a media briefing.

“While each cabin has been designed individually, they are united by the same ambition to make the experience more comfortable, flexible and rewarding for our customers,” he adds in a Nov 6 statement. “SIA’s next-generation long-haul cabin products will ensure that our customers travel more comfortably than before and have greater control over their in-flight experience.”

The products, Lee says, were originally designed for the Boeing 777-9, which was delayed “for many years”. In that time, the team reviewed its overall product strategy and decided to include the changes on the Airbus A350 long-haul range, as well. The new designs were supposed to be launched on the Boeing 777-9 as early as 2021.

According to SIA, the new products came after the airline surveyed over 5,000 frequent travellers, customers, staff and industry experts since 2018.

See also: IndiGo offering lie-flat beds on Airbus A350 to attract long-haul business flyers

Despite the delay, Lee believes the airline’s feedback and research remains “relevant” and as such, it has a product that its customers “will truly enjoy”. In that time, the airline has also reviewed and improved on “finer elements” within the design.

He adds that the group remains “very confident” that the key design elements on how it made the seats as well as their features are “still relevant and important”.

See also: JetBlue shares soar after it vows to return to profitability

In first class, passengers will enjoy a “luxurious private sanctuary” with curved sliding doors for privacy. The divider is fully retractable, which allows passengers in the two centre seats to enjoy one enlarged space. Their seats - 23 inches wide apiece - can also be converted into a two-seater sofa or a double bed measuring 80 inches long and a combined 60 inches wide. The double beds are believed to be the largest in commercial aviation, said SIA. The Boeing 777-9 will have six seats while the Airbus A350-900 ULR

Passengers in business class will appreciate the enhanced seat ergonomics with coordinated reclining movements, an adjustable lumbar and leg support. The seats transform into full-flat beds, which measure 79 inches long and 24 inches wide (for the Boeing 777-9) and 22 inches (for both Airbus aircraft). Certain centre seats can be configured as “companion beds” when the dividers are lowered. The Boeing 777-9 will have 54 seats, the Airbus A350-900 will have 42, while the Airbus A350-900 ULR will have 70 seats.

The new seats in premium economy now have 40-inch pitches, from 38 inches previously. Seats come with a four-way adjustable headrest and leg rest with an adjustable foot rest. The Boeing 777-9 will have 36 seats. When asked if SIA was considering more seats within the cabin class, senior vice president for product experience, Yeoh Phee Teik says the number will remain unchanged for now, while a spokesperson said the decision depends on what the airline’s customers value and are invested in accordingly.

The new economy class seats are designed to “enhance comfort” with “Ergonomic cushioning, improved knee and shin clearance, and adjustable headrest for greater comfort throughout the flight”. There will be 204 seats on the Boeing 777-9 aircraft.

Asked why the airline chose a “minor refresh” of the premium economy and economy seats instead of installing new ones, given that the retrofitted aircraft are expected to fly into the late 2030s, Lee says the decision was based on a review of “various factors”. On adding newer features such as USB or Bluetooth, Lee adds that it is something the airline will consider in future.

The refurbishment will also not add any weight to the aircraft, shares Ong Wah Li, vice president, product experience.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

On whether the group means to focus on its long-haul flights, Lee says that is “not the case”; the group is focused on “every aspect” of its network, whether it’s long-, medium- or short-haul flights.

The situation, he adds, stemmed from the introduction of the Boeing 777-9 long-haul fleet as well as the group’s decision to retrofit its long-haul Airbus A350 fleet. That said, the group’s medium-haul fleet experienced a “major overhaul” during Covid, when SIA decided to phase out its Airbus A330s and introduced Airbus A350s and Boeing 787s to the medium-haul fleet. The short-haul Boeing 737s also “received investments” when the group changed its business class seats to lie-flat seats compared to the reclining-only product, previously.

On being one of the last carriers to conduct cabin refurbishments, Lee says the group does not comment on timelines but attributed the latest launch to the delay of the Boeing 777-9.

On funding, Lee notes that the group was “fortunate” to be “well-supported” by its customers, which therefore led to a “very strong cash balance”.

For the 1QFY2027 ended June, the group reported cash reserves of $10.48 billion. Total cash and bank balances stood at $9.1 billion.

SIA, on Oct 14 and Oct 22, announced a new range of in-flight amenities and enhanced in-flight entertainment. For the first time, “sleeper suits” or pyjamas will be offered to business class passengers. This marks a turnaround from when then senior vice president of sales and marketing, Campbell Wilson, said during the relaunch of the non-stop flights from Singapore to New York in October 2018, that “most people don’t actually use pyjamas on board an aircraft. Most travellers bring a change of clothes if they wish to or indeed just sleep in the clothes they have. We obviously monitor, but at this juncture we’ve not seen a really strong demand.”

When asked, Yeoh says the decision to introduce pyjamas in business class was made after receiving feedback from customers. It was also a “business decision” that the group undertook.

Other upgrades include the new SilverKris lounges across its network and in Singapore, which cost the group $130 million.

The launch, says SIA CEO Goh Choon Phong, marks “another major milestone” for the airline. “Our customers experience SIA as one seamless journey and this significant investment is designed to deliver greater comfort, choice and convenience at every stage.”

He adds that the launch is not an “endpoint” but another step in its “continuous pursuit to earn and retain the trust and loyalty of our customers and reinforce our leadership in the airline industry.”

SIA will be releasing its 1HFY2027 results after trading hours on Nov 11.

title: Yen regains haven appeal as AI rout sends investors to safety
article:
(Nov 6): The yen held onto gains on Friday after a sell-off in US technology shares drove investors towards safer assets, a shift that strategists expect will provide further support to the currency.

The Japanese currency rose 0.2% to 157.34 per dollar in early Asian trading after strengthening as much as 0.6% to 157.54 on Thursday, when it outperformed all of its Group-of-10 (G10) peers. The advance came as concerns over the outlook for artificial intelligence (AI) investment following a Democratic sweep in this week’s US midterm elections triggered a sharp sell-off on Wall Street.

The latest move adds to signs that the yen may be regaining some of its traditional haven characteristics. It briefly strengthened to 156.08 per greenback last month during an earlier bout of technology-stock weakness before giving back much of the advance. Goldman Sachs Group Inc strategists have said the Japanese currency is becoming a more effective hedge against an AI-driven market shock.

“If the AI trade continues to unwind, investors will be looking for somewhere to go,” said Sarah Ying, the head of foreign exchange strategy at CIBC Capital Markets. “We suspect that demand for haven currencies would rise,” including the yen or franc.

She expects the yen to strengthen to 148 against the dollar by the end of 2027, a more-than-6% rise from current levels, as investors flee dollar-denominated assets.

See also: Pound strength highest since Brexit vote ahead of BOE hike

The Japanese currency has historically benefitted during periods of market stress, but that relationship weakened in recent years as wide US-Japan interest-rate differentials and persistent Japanese investment overseas encouraged investors to sell the currency even during bouts of risk aversion.

Dominic Bunning, the head of G10 foreign exchange strategy at Nomura International plc, said the firm remains long on the Japanese yen against the dollar, calling it the “consistent best foreign exchange trade” in an environment in which equities and yields are both declining.

The yen also stands to benefit if Japanese money managers rotate more of their investments out of foreign bond markets and into local ones as the Bank of Japan (BOJ) raises interest rates, he said. He expects further BOJ rate hikes to help sustain the trade.

See also: Franc, yen emerge as FX winners as US midterms weaken dollar

The central bank will announce its next policy decision on Dec 18, with overnight index swaps pricing in a 76% chance of a rate hike by then.

Decades of ultra-low Japanese interest rates encouraged the country’s insurers, pension funds and other investors to build large holdings of overseas assets in search of higher returns. As domestic yields rise, keeping more money at home — even without outright sales of existing foreign holdings — could reduce a persistent source of yen selling.

The dollar, meanwhile, has received little of the haven demand that might normally accompany such a sharp equity sell-off. A Bloomberg gauge of the US currency edged just 0.1% higher on Thursday even as tech stocks suffered their steepest decline since 2020.

“The yen is benefitting from the return of safe-haven demand amid equity volatility,” said Nathan Thooft, a senior portfolio manager at Manulife Investment Management. “The dollar has the opposite problem: so much US exceptionalism is now tied to AI that any crack in that story can quickly become a dollar story, too.”

title: OpenAI to change how it handles data centres after outcry
article:
(Nov 6): OpenAI said it will avoid non-disclosure agreements when it negotiates data centre deals and ensure residents don’t pay for the electricity to power those projects, part of a framework the company believes should be adopted into laws governing the expansion of artificial intelligence (AI).

The series of commitments was released on Thursday, just two days after voters across the US backed candidates at all levels of government who support curbs on data centres and greater oversight of AI.

In a so-called National Community Compact, the company pledges to provide clear data about the potential community impacts of issues including noise, water and energy use. OpenAI also promised to reduce power usage during peak times, send electricity back to the grid and set local hiring goals, assuming the local workforce allows for it. The AI lab will also publicly report on its progress toward keeping these commitments.

“Households shouldn’t bear the costs of powering data centres,” OpenAI said in the policy document. “Instead, compute campus investment should help expand and modernise America’s energy grid, strengthen reliability, and deliver broader benefits to consumers.”

OpenAI said it had planned the announcement prior to the election returns and has been working on it for months. It combines some measures the AI research lab has already announced in its data centre projects in areas such as Georgia and adds others that stem from conversations with residents and officials in Georgia, Ohio, Texas and other states, said Chris Lehane, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer.

“Certainly a number of them are places that have been particularly impacted by the globalisation of the last 20, 30 years, and for a lot of really good reasons these folks have been really burned by companies and others in the past,” Lehane said.

See also: AI and technology must support agents, not replace them: SIEA president

Voters across the US gave the data centre boom a clear thumbs down Tuesday night. Gina Hinojosa, elected on Tuesday as the first Democratic governor in Texas in more than three decades, has called for an immediate moratorium on data centre development. Other Democratic gubernatorial victories from Georgia to Ohio and Pennsylvania could leave half of proposed AI data centre additions across the US vulnerable to stricter local scrutiny and pushback. At least 45 projects valued at US$68 billion ($87 billion) were disrupted in some fashion by local opposition in the second quarter of 2026, according to Data Center Watch, a research group.

With data centres becoming increasingly politically unpopular, it’s possible some OpenAI projects will be delayed, Lehane said.

“The scale that we are building at there’s just going to be a lot of types of things, questions at different levels, state level, local level, that you have to address,” he said. “People are certainly going to be mindful of how voters express themselves.”

See also: What to know about the Anthropic IPO

OpenAI has been speaking with candidates — incumbents and challengers — over the past few months to share many of its ideas about how to make data centres beneficial to residents, Lehane said, while declining to specify which candidates.

“If you are going to go into a community and you are going to want to build in that community, you do have to do it with the community and get the community input,” Lehane said. “And the fact that people have expressed themselves at the ballot box in the way that they have, is an important message that people have to listen to and react to and respond to. This is how democracy is supposed to work.”

title: Hackers paid US$15 to drain US$2.5 billion from Binance in one hit
article:
(Nov 6): The hackers who stole US$6.3 billion from Binance last week found a way to take 40% of the stolen cryptocurrency in one hit, reducing their chances of being caught in the act, and it cost them just US$15.

An examination of transactions recorded on the Ethereum blockchain shows how the thieves weaponised a feature designed to make crypto wallets easier to use. It allows an account to give software permission to move money on its behalf, rather than requiring separate authorizations for each transfer.

The hackers paid about US$15 in network fees to put that permission in place, then used it to take roughly US$2.5 billion in a single transaction — 40% of the total amount stolen — according to security firm Blockaid.

On Tuesday, Binance itself outlined an elaborate timeline in which infiltrators used phony job postings to deceive an engineer into downloading malicious code. It was a “sophisticated, multi-stage campaign,” according to the exchange, replete with social engineering, compromised devices and AI techniques.

Once inside, the hackers targeted a “hot wallet” known as Binance 14, which the exchange uses to process customer withdrawals, records on the Etherscan analytics platform show. This wallet is a bit like an online cash register, and because Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange, it regularly holds large pools of Ether, stablecoins and dozens of other digital tokens.

See also: ING said to be seller of US$500 mil data centre loan portfolio — Bloomberg

Moving so many different assets would ordinarily require a series of separate transfers, each taking time and creating another chance for security systems to spot something unusual.

But an Ethereum software upgrade known as EIP-7702 offered a shortcut.

See also: Apple’s tight-lipped CEO John Ternus fails to inspire

Before it was implemented in May 2025, a basic crypto wallet was more akin to a checking account, where the owner generally had to sign off on each transaction. The upgrade added something closer to an autopay function, letting a wallet give software the ability to act on its behalf and bundle several actions together.

At about 8:20 p.m. UTC on Oct 29, the hackers submitted instructions using a valid signature from the Binance 14 wallet telling the Ethereum network to let attacker-controlled code act on the account’s behalf, according to Blockaid. It’s at this point that they paid the routine network processing fee to put that authority in place.

That transaction moved no money, it simply told Ethereum to let the hackers’ software act for the wallet.

“The program does one thing: when its owner asks, it empties the wallet into an address of the owner’s choosing,” blockchain research firm Tibane Labs said in a report.

Three and a half minutes later, the hackers triggered the trap. Operating under the new permissions, the attacker’s software moved roughly US$2.5 billion in a single transaction, according to Blockaid. The haul included 167,464 Ether and more than 60 other tokens, led by US$1.6 billion in Tether’s USDT stablecoin.

“In an attack, the defender wants to slow the attacker down,” said Dan Caspi, co-founder and chief technology officer at Hypernative. “EIP-7702 helped the hackers move faster and maintain control of the wallet even after Binance detected the breach.”

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Because the permission lived on Ethereum, Binance turning off withdrawals or shutting down its hot-wallet services did not automatically cancel it, according to the exchange’s incident report.

With deposits unaffected and continuing to flow into Binance 14, the hackers could still initiate transfers. They ultimately used the same permission to take roughly $3.6 billion, including the initial $2.5 billion haul, with $823 million pulled from another Binance account and four subsequent sweeps of Binance 14, according to a report from blockchain intelligence firm Elliptic.

A Binance spokesperson confirmed that EIP-7702 “played a significant role” in the hack and said the exchange has taken steps to address the risk it exposed.

“We have revoked the affected delegation, rebuilt the affected wallet infrastructure, and updated our signing and monitoring controls to address this class of authorization risk,” they said. “This includes stricter policies around delegation-type transactions, enhanced behavioral monitoring, additional transaction-level controls, and emergency revocation procedures.”

Binance has also strengthened enforcement of access controls so the access path used cannot be repeated, the spokesperson said, adding “user funds remain protected, and Binance has absorbed the financial impact of this incident.”

The episode shows how tools meant to make crypto accounts simpler can also make a breach far more damaging once an intruder gets inside.

The FBI has attributed the attack, the largest cryptocurrency theft on record, to North Korea. Pyongyang has denied any involvement.

title: ING said to be seller of US$500 mil data centre loan portfolio — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 6): Dutch bank ING is putting up for sale a roughly US$500 million portfolio of data centre loans all at once, according to people familiar with the matter. The rare auction comes just days after a Democratic sweep of the US midterm elections raised doubts about the future of many of the projects.

The bank is taking offers for a dozen loans via a so-called bids-wanted-in-competition process, the people added, asking not to be identified because the information is private. The loans for sale include a US$25 million slice backing a massive data centre site that’s part of OpenAI, SoftBank Group Corp and Oracle Corp’s joint Stargate project in New Mexico. It’s the location where Oracle sent the developer a notice citing force majeure.

It is also looking to offload debt tied to operators such as Vantage Data Centers and CyrusOne, said the people. Bids on the loans are due Nov 19 and must be at least US$10 million in size, they added.

The auction, among the first of its kind that exclusively contains data centre debt, underscores the market pessimism that has erupted over the AI buildout in the wake of the US elections. In Texas, where many developers have a presence, the Democratic governor-elect has called for an immediate moratorium on construction for the projects.

The Nasdaq 100 closed 6.4% lower Thursday, wiping out US$2.3 trillion in value and extending weeks of concerns from Wall Street investors who have been retreating from the AI trade. In the high-yield market, junk bonds tied to data centre developers or projects, including CoreWeave Inc and Galaxy Digital Inc, saw some of the biggest declines.

See also: Apple’s tight-lipped CEO John Ternus fails to inspire

Wall Street is broadly contending with the risk that the credit market is nearing the limit for how much AI debt it can absorb amid questions of whether revenue can justify the breathtaking spending.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc and Apollo Global Management Inc are looking to syndicate portions of the largest chip financing on record tied to SpaceX, Bloomberg reported this week. They committed to the deal in October before pricing it, and now face the prospect of the market turning against them.
